messages:
sam_cs: FYI we have a customer (Finlytics) reporting rerank API returning negative and >1 scores in the same response — they expect 0-1 probabilities. They pasted a snippet, asking if the SDK changed.

maria_support: Can you paste the exact response body? is this rerank v1 or v2?

sam_cs: Pasted below (redacted keys):
```json
{
  "query": "find matching policy",
  "candidates": ["docA", "docB"],
  "scores": [ -3.21, 2.14 ]
}
```

maria_support: thanks. That looks like raw logits are being returned. We normally convert to probabilities in the client. Did they call the endpoint with ?raw_scores=true or use the internal SDK option?

dmitri_ml: Quick context: our reranker can output different score types depending on model and params — "logit" (raw), "prob" (softmax normalized), or "score_normalized" (custom scaling). Historically the hosted API defaulted to returning normalized probabilities, but a recent change to the model-adapters layer meant some lightweight models return logits unless a normalization flag is passed.

ashley_research: Repro steps I used locally:
1) call curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/rerank -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"query":"q","candidates":["a","b"],"params":{"score_type":"logit"}}'
2) got [-1.2, 0.4] as expected.
3) call with params {"score_type":"prob"} -> [0.31,0.69] (softmax).

maria_support: So the fix for Finlytics is likely client-side: tell them to set params.score_type=prob or softmax in SDK. Also update their docs to interpret negative values as logits, not probabilities.

sam_cs: Customer says they never set that param. Is default behavior documented anywhere?

dmitri_ml: We messed up — default was supposed to be "prob" but a new adapter that optimizes for latency returns logits by default for smaller models. I'll open a rollback/patch. In the meantime we should: 1) tell support how to translate logits to probs (softmax), 2) surface a server-side compatibility header.

maria_support: Short customer reply I can send: "We see raw model scores (logits) — negative numbers are expected for logits. To convert to 0-1 probabilities apply softmax across the candidate set. Alternatively, call the rerank endpoint with params.score_type=\"prob\" to get normalized outputs."

sam_cs: Customer asked for a one-liner explanation of what the numbers mean in their UI (they want to show a little label). Any suggestions?

dmitri_ml: One-liner: "Scores may be raw model logits (unbounded) or normalized probabilities (0–1). If you're seeing negatives, those are logits — convert with softmax for probabilities."

ashley_research: Also add a short example they can display: input two logits [-3.21,2.14] -> softmax -> [0.018,0.982] so docB is ~98% likely.

maria_support: I'm sending that now. Also created a support ticket to notify eng-runtime to revert default to normalized outputs and to add an explicit response field "score_type" to every rerank response.

ops_bot: Incident created: RUNTIME-4821 - revert default rerank score_type to "prob". Priority: P2.

sam_cs: Thanks. Can we also add a short note in the API docs and an SDK patch that forces prob by default? The customer will want a change window.

dmitri_ml: Yes, I'll PR a small adapter change to set default score_type to 'prob' and add response metadata. ETA EOD today for patch + tests.

maria_support: Great — I'll follow up with the customer once the rollback is confirmed and include the softmax snippet and explanation.

sam_cs: Closing the loop: customer appreciated the explanation and applied a client-side softmax as a stopgap. They asked for a stable default in the hosted API.
